All four EQE values so far are near zero. I'll use XRD to look for a different phase in the middle of the line.

content.text:
I've submitted **index 0 (Sb fraction 0.031)** as best, but the campaign didn't find an active photoanode. All five EQE readings were at about the noise floor, so this choice is only marginally better than the others.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.031 | 0.00035 |
| 4 | 0.056 | 0.00025 |
| 9 | 0.127 | −0.00037 |
| 16 | 0.307 | 0.00013 |
| 22 | 0.499 | 0.00026 |

**What the XRD showed** (4 of 5 scans used):
- **Bi-rich end:** the films are crystalline. At Sb 0.056 the best match is a fluorite-type Bi₂O₃ phase (mp-23195, similarity 0.81).
- **Middle of the line:** that phase's peaks get weaker at Sb 0.27 and 0.40. I found no ternary phase at either point (neither BiSbO₄ nor Bi₃SbO₇).
- **High-Sb end:** at Sb 0.66 only the FTO substrate peaks remain, so the film looks amorphous.

**Why index 0:** it had the highest EQE, and it sits at the most crystalline Bi₂O₃ end, which is the most plausible place for any activity. The differences between readings are too small to show a real trend, though.

**What's still unmeasured:** EQE between Sb 0.16 and 0.45 (only index 16 was tested there) and anything above Sb 0.50. XRD suggests the high-Sb end is amorphous and unlikely to be active, but I can't rule out a narrow active window somewhere on the line.
